title: Four young Israelis built ICQ, the instant messaging software, and sold it to AOL

trailer.text: ICQ, software that made it possible to know at any moment whether friends were connected to the Web and free for a chat, was created in 1996 by Mirabilis, an Israeli software company.
Mirabilis was founded in mid-1996 by four Israeli partners: Sefi Vigiser, Yair Goldfinger, Arik Vardi and Amnon Amir.
The software was distributed for free on the Internet and without marketing, and by February 1998 it had reached eight million users worldwide.
In June 1998, AOL announced the completion of its acquisition of Mirabilis, at a sum that may reach $407 million.
According to JTA, this was the biggest-ever foreign acquisition of an Israeli software company.

stations.title: Four friends and a ping pong table

paragraphs.text: Four young men used to meet for ping pong games in Amnon Amir's house: Yair Goldfinger, Sefi Vigiser, Amir and Arik Vardi.
They were looking for an idea for a joint project.
According to ComputerBase, the four were unemployed at the time and were looking for a way out of the situation.
According to Globes, before ICQ most users were dependent on the IRC server, with an unstable chat system.
The first idea they chose was to connect pager networks to the Internet.
In mid-1996, the four founded Mirabilis.
In 1998, Globes gave their ages: Amnon Amir, 24, Sefi Vigiser, 25, Yair Goldfinger, 26, and Arik Vardi, 27.
According to JTA, Yossi Vardi and the programmers founded the company with an investment of $3.2 million.
According to a book cited in Calcalist, while trying to solve the pager problem they decided to develop a tool that would notify each of them when the others were online.
Globes wrote that Mirabilis was the first to put such a product on the market.
Vigiser said that the company's "submarine" stage started in Sunnyvale, California.
There they sat around the clock in a small room and worked on the software.
According to Vigiser, even before the move to the United States, which was meant for further development, the team had a working product after four months of working in secret, almost underground.
The software was called ICQ, and it enabled rapid messaging between Internet surfers.
An ICQ user could know at any moment whether his friends, real or virtual, were connected to the Web and free for a chat.
According to Vardi, ICQ was launched in November 1996.
Vigiser, to Globes: in a small room in Sunnyvale, California
Globes wrote that Mirabilis was the first to introduce a distribution method that was dubbed word of mouse.
Users could distribute the software from within it, with the click of a button.
ICQ spread as people encouraged their friends to join, so that they could communicate with them.
Vigiser said that the company does not invest in marketing and has no sales personnel.
He added that it does not take part in exhibitions and has no public relations activities.
According to JTA, the software was distributed for free on the Internet.
According to the book cited in Calcalist, shortly after its launch ICQ acquired nearly half a million users.
The first competitor appeared about six months later, and by then the company already had 850 thousand users, forming a critical mass.
In the three months before the interview in Globes, ICQ was in first place in the number of downloads, and at that time the number of downloads stood at 240 thousand a week.
In February 1998, Globes wrote that the software had been distributed to eight million users worldwide.
According to Globes, their number was then growing by about 20% a month.
According to Mirabilis, 1.3 million people used the software daily.
At peak hours, the Mirabilis infrastructure served 370 thousand users simultaneously.
That month, Mirabilis had sixty employees.
Six of them worked in support in the United States, and the rest in Israel.
The company was not yet generating income, and the main direction for income was not clear.
Vigiser said he would like to see the program become standard within two years, with 40 million users worldwide.
On June 9, 1998, Globes reported that AOL had announced the completion of its acquisition of Mirabilis, at a sum that may reach $407 million.
According to Globes, AOL will pay $287 million in cash for full ownership, plus an additional sum dependent on the company's performance.
JTA reported that this was the biggest-ever foreign acquisition of an Israeli software company.
According to JTA, Mirabilis then had 70 employees and no revenues.
According to Vardi, by then nearly 13 million people had downloaded ICQ, without the company spending money on advertising or public relations.
According to Israeli analysts, AOL could use ICQ Web sites as a springboard for selling advertisements and offering new services.
According to Globes, analyst Mary Meeker of Morgan Stanley determined that ICQ was worth more than most of the other Internet companies in the world.
According to Globes, the shareholders also included well-known Israeli private investors, among them Michael and Binjamin Jesselson.
According to Globes, each of the two held shares valued at $7.5 million.
CEO Sefi Vigiser said that the founding group will continue to head the development of future generations of ICQ.

stations.title: The exit and what came after

paragraphs.text: According to the book The Israeli Mind, an excerpt of which was published in Calcalist, pictures of the founders adorned the newspapers and ignited the imagination of tens of thousands of computer enthusiasts.
According to the book, the deal turned "exit" into a legitimate Hebrew word.
In 1999, Globes wrote that this is the high-tech deal most recalled by the majority of Israelis, and that it brought Israel the most public relations.
According to Globes, Mirabilis became the emblem of Israeli high-tech, in Israel and overseas.
Globes wrote that the flourishing of start-ups in Israel is closely linked to Mirabilis.
Globes also wrote that they should mainly be remembered as the ones who beat Microsoft.
Under AOL ownership, ICQ reached about 100 million users at its peak.
According to the book cited in Calcalist, AOL later sold ICQ to the Russian company DST, and the Israeli development center was closed in 2012.
In May 2024, Calcalist reported that after 28 years of activity, ICQ would be shut down in a month, and on June 26, 2024, AFP reported that the service had indeed shut down.

According to a Form 8-K that AOL filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, on April 28, 2010, AOL signed a Securities Purchase Agreement with Digital Sky Technologies for the sale of the ICQ business.
Arik's father, Dr. Yossi Vardi, joined the group shortly after it was founded.
He handled the company's business aspects and strategy.
According to Jüdische Allgemeine, Yossi Vardi was the first CEO of Mirabilis.
According to the newspaper, Vardi invested several hundred thousand dollars of his own money in the company.
Globes described a group of young people led by a father figure with a successful business mind.
According to Globes, the group fell upon an accidental situation, a holiday in the Sinai desert, and conquered the world.
According to BasicThinking, Yair Goldfinger is co-founder and CEO of AppCard, a customer loyalty platform.
Globes criticized ICQ for setting a world trend of companies with no business model, whose aim was to build a database of names and email addresses.
ComputerBase noted that ICQ was criticized as adware.
According to ComputerBase, it tended to change homepages and search engines and to install browser extensions without the user's consent.
According to BasicThinking, in 2023 an investigation by the Brazilian magazine Núcleo Jornalismo revealed that ICQ was used to distribute child pornography, because of lax moderation rules.
According to Jüdische Allgemeine, it is often claimed that selling high-tech companies abroad stifles the development of large companies in Israel.
Yossi Vardi replied in Globes that such large companies already exist in Israel, and their names are Intel Israel, Microsoft Israel and Cisco Israel.

versions.says: Vigiser, to Globes: a working product after four months
The book cited in Calcalist: 18 months of development in a basement
Jüdische Allgemeine: about three years of development

disagreements.question: How much was the additional sum, beyond $287 million?

versions.says: Globes, in the same article: an additional $120 million
The book cited in Calcalist: $120 million contingent on meeting goals

disagreements.question: How much did each founder receive from the deal?

versions.says: Globes: around $90 million for each of the four main shareholders
JTA: about $60 million each, out of the $287 million

disagreements.question: How many users did ICQ have at the time of the deal in 1998?

versions.says: Vardi, according to JTA: nearly 13 million people had downloaded the software
AOL, in its annual report to the SEC: 12 million registered trial users at the date of acquisition, about half of them active

disagreements.question: When did ICQ reach its peak number of users?

versions.says: The book cited in Calcalist: about 100 million registered users in 2001
BasicThinking: more than 100 million users already in 2000

disagreements.question: What was Yossi Vardi's role at Mirabilis?

versions.says: Jüdische Allgemeine (2021): the first CEO of Mirabilis
Globes (February 1998): the company has no general manager; Vardi handles business aspects and strategy

claims.text: ComputerBase ציין ש-ICQ זכתה לביקורת כאדוור: היא נטתה לשנות דפי בית ומנועי חיפוש ולהתקין תוספי דפדפן ללא הסכמת המשתמש.
claims.quote: da das Programm dazu neigte, ganz ohne Einwilligung des Anwenders, Startseiten und Suchmaschinen zu manipulieren und ungefragt Browser-Erweiterungen zu installieren.

claims.text: לפי BasicThinking, ב-2023 חשף מחקר של המגזין הברזילאי Núcleo Jornalismo שבגלל כללי פיקוח רופפים שימשה ICQ להפצת פורנוגרפיית ילדים.
claims.quote: Eine Untersuchung des brasilianischen Nachrichtenmagazins Núcleo Jornalismo ergab 2023 jedoch, dass ICQ aufgrund lascher Moderationsrichtlinien zum freien Austausch von Kinderpornografie genutzt wurde.

claims.text: לפי העיתון, נטען לעיתים קרובות שמכירת חברות היי-טק לחו"ל חונקת את התפתחות החברות הגדולות בישראל.
claims.quote: Nur würde so die Entwicklung von großen Unternehmen im eigenen Land abgewürgt, heißt es oft.

claims.text: יוסי ורדי השיב בגלובס שחברות גדולות כאלה כבר קיימות בישראל, ושמותיהן אינטל ישראל, מיקרוסופט ישראל וסיסקו ישראל.
claims.quote: Die gibt es doch längst. Nur heißen sie Intel Israel, Microsoft Israel und Cisco Israel.

claims.text: לפי הספר, הארבעה ננעלו במרתף ל-18 חודשי פיתוח אינטנסיביים ויצאו עם ICQ.
claims.quote: locked themselves up in a basement for 18 hectic development months, and emerged with ICQ.

claims.text: לפי Jüdische Allgemeine, ארבעת הסטודנטים מתל אביב השיקו את ICQ בנובמבר 1996 לאחר כשלוש שנות פיתוח.
claims.quote: Yair Goldfinger, Arik Vardi sowie Sefi Vigiser und Amnon Amir, vier Studenten aus Tel Aviv, im November 1996 nach rund drei Jahren Entwicklungsarbeit mit ICQ an den Start gingen

claims.text: לפי הספר, ביוני 1998 נחתם חוזה למכירת מירביליס ל-AOL תמורת 287 מיליון דולר במזומן ועוד 120 מיליון דולר שתלויים בעמידה ביעדים.
claims.quote: In June 1998, a contract was signed according to which Mirabilis was sold to AOL for $287 million in cash and another $120 million were contingent on meeting the business goals.

claims.text: לפי גלובס, כל אחד מארבעת בעלי המניות העיקריים יקבל סביב 90 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: Each of the four main shareholders will receive around $90 million.

claims.text: לפי JTA, כל אחד מארבעת המייסדים העיקריים יקבל כ-60 מיליון דולר מתוך 287 המיליון.
claims.quote: each of the four principle founders will receive approximately $60 million of the $287 million price.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, בכל מקרה בני הצוות היו צעירים שהפכו לשווים יותר מ-100 מיליון דולר כל אחד.
claims.quote: It was hard to believe that those young men, all in their early 20’s, were suddenly worth more than $100 million each.

claims.text: ComputerBase כתב שבתקופת העסקה כבר היו ל-ICQ יותר מ-100 מיליון משתמשים בעולם.
claims.quote: Zu diesem Zeitpunkt hatte des Instant Messenger bereits eine weltweite Nutzerschaft von deutlich mehr als 100 Millionen Anwendern

claims.text: לפי BasicThinking, בשנת 2000 מנתה השירות יותר מ-100 מיליון משתמשים והיה מוביל שוק.
claims.quote: Im Jahr 2000 zählte der Dienst mehr als 100 Millionen User und war Marktführer.

claims.text: לפי דיווח 8-K ש-AOL הגישה לרשות ניירות הערך האמריקאית, ב-28 באפריל 2010 חתמה AOL על הסכם רכישת ניירות ערך עם Digital Sky Technologies למכירת פעילות ICQ.
claims.quote: As previously announced, on April 28, 2010, AOL Inc., (the "Company") entered into a Securities Purchase Agreement

claims.text: ICQ התפשטה כשאנשים עודדו את חבריהם להצטרף, כדי שיוכלו לתקשר איתם.
claims.quote: simply sent messages to friends, inviting them to install the software

claims.text: ICQ התפשטה כשאנשים עודדו את חבריהם להצטרף, כדי שיוכלו לתקשר איתם.
claims.quote: ICQ had the advantage of actually being viral, spreading by word of mouth.

claims.text: לפי ספר שמובא בכלכליסט, בניסיון לפתור את בעיית הזימוניות הם החליטו לפתח כלי שיודיע לכל אחד מהם מתי האחרים מחוברים לרשת.
claims.quote: decided to develop a tool that would notify each of them when the others are online

claims.text: לפי הספר "The Israeli Mind", שקטע ממנו פורסם בכלכליסט, תמונות המייסדים קישטו את העיתונים והציתו את דמיונם של עשרות אלפי חובבי מחשבים.
claims.quote: ignited the imagination of tens of thousands computer aficionados
